new_statements.relation_note: No catalog record (in_catalog false). Agrees with the one statement held by the project, Schanely 1965 'The Phonemes of Gaikunti' sec. 5.3.2 ('usually falls on the second syllable in words of more than one syllable'), of which this OPD line is a near-verbatim digest (the OPD's bibliography cites Schanely 1965). It adds nothing new (no weight, secondary stress or exceptions) and omits Schanely's /a/-attraction remark.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the second syllable of polysyllabic words ('usually'); the OPD gives no phonemic role to tone, stress or length (the heading lumps them and the only statement is this placement rule). The sentence is a condensation of Schanely 1965 sec. 5.3.2.
new_statements.exceptions: only the hedge 'usually'; the OPD drops Schanely's remark that stress is sometimes attracted to the low vowel /a/; no exceptions listed
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD describes 'Gaikundi (Gaikunti, Gai Kundi) [GBF]', located at Ambunti, East Sepik Province (Ndu family), drawing on Schanely 1965 (Gaikunti, 'dialect of Sawos') and the 1975 Sauu/Nate Gaikundi dictionary; the archive title's 'Ontena' does not occur in the document and looks like a cataloguing slip (Ontena is a Gadsup village; SIL 42439 is the separate Gadsup-Ontena OPD). Same language and, as far as the sources say, the same variety as the statement held by the project.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no prior statement for gaik1242; this is the first placement statement found (marked 'refines' only because there is nothing to agree or disagree with). Note the wording of 5.3.1-5.3.2 is nearly identical to Staalsen 1966 on Iatmul (Nyaura) ('Stress is sometimes related to and predictable by the vowel..'), i.e. an SIL New Guinea template of the period; the second-syllable default is Schanely's own addition for Gaikunti.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-phonemic (not contrastive); in polysyllables it usually falls on the second syllable, with the low vowel /a/ sometimes attracting/predicting stress instead; vowel length accompanies the stressed syllable; there is no lexical tone, pitch functions only as intonation, and sentence stress (high pitch) overrides word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: 'Stress is sometimes related to and predictable by the low vowel /a/' (i.e. /a/ can pull stress off the default second syllable); no examples with stress marks are given; monosyllables trivially excluded ('words of more than one syllable').
new_statements.identity_note: Schanely 1965 describes 'Gaikunti' ('place talk', his own coinage) as spoken in Wereman village, one of three villages 5-10 miles east of Pagwi, north of the Sepik and south of the Wosera, c. 700 speakers, bordering the Torembi ('Sawos') group to the east; this is the variety Glottolog files as gaik1242 Gaikundi (Laycock 1973 entry 91 'Sawos': 'L. Schanely has prepared an unpublished phonemic statement of one Sawos dialect which he calls Gaikunti'). The unfetched 2011 OPD is titled 'Gaikundi-Ontena'; 'Ontena' is otherwise a Gadsup dialect name (Eastern Highlands), so the OPD's identity should be checked against its own first page if it is ever obtained, although SIL's metadata lists its subject language as Gaikundi [gbf].
